I've been farming these 10.1 mu for most of my life, so I don't start fresh each year — I do what worked last year and adjust a little. My land sits in the wheat-maize belt, but I keep about 3 mu in cotton because the price has held up and I already have the experience with it. The rest, about 7 mu, goes wheat in winter and maize in summer like everyone around me.

For wheat, I plant an improved variety — Jimai or something similar that the seed dealer in town recommends, same as my neighbor Old Wang uses. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (about 50 jin, 15-15-15) per mu as base fertilizer before sowing, then top-dress with urea at jointing — about 20 jin per mu. That comes out to roughly 17 kg nitrogen per mu. I know the extension person said I could use less, but a bad wheat harvest would cost me more than the extra urea. Phosphorus about 8 kg, potassium about 7 kg. I water 4 times — before winter, at green-up, at jointing, and at filling. Well water is not free but the pump is mine. I spray 2 times, once for aphids and once for rust if I see it. I expect about 500 kg per mu — that's what I got last two years.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, every year. I broadcast compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at big trumpet stage. Total nitrogen about 18 kg, phosphorus 6, potassium 6. I irrigate 2 times if the rain is short. One spray for corn borer. Yield 550 kg per mu is normal.

For cotton on 3.1 mu, I use improved Bt seed so I don't spray as much for bollworm. Cotton likes potassium, so I give more — about 10 kg. Nitrogen 14 kg, phosphorus 7. Four irrigations through the season. I still spray 4 times for aphids, mirids, and sometimes bollworm late. 280 kg seed cotton per mu is a decent year.

I plough for cotton but use rotary tillage for wheat and maize — saves money and time, and my son helps with the machinery service.
